And he shall judge among many people •and rebuke strong nations afar off; and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks; nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.” Micah iv. 2, 3.

Elder Bruce R. Mc Conkie explained: "It was of these that Zechariah prophesied when as part of a longer Messianic utterance, he spoke of 'prisoners of hope'; it was of these that he gave assurance that 'the Lord their God shall save them.' He gives the Messianic message in these words: 'By the blood of the covenant'-that is, because of the gospel covenant, which is efficacious because of the shedding of the blood of Christ-'I have sent forth thy prisoners out of the pit wherein is no water.' (Zech. 9:11-16.) 'Wherein is no water'-how aptly and succinctly this crystallizes the thought that the saving water, which is baptism, is an earthly ordinance and cannot be performed by spirit beings while they dwell in the spirit world. Did not Paul say in this same connection, 'What shall they do which are baptized for the dead, if the dead rise not at all? why are they then baptized for the dead?' (1 Cor. 15:29.)

notes.text: The first and last articles of faith of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints embody principles, large in their concept of life. These two statements of religion deal with the most important problems of the soul, and they solve in a general way how man may enter into a divine world. Perhaps the majority of mankind is not yet ready for such a presentation of religion; but it is through some such conception as the thought of these two statements that mankind will grasp the meaning of life and its ultimate end. notes.text: Jesus Christ is the true shepherd of men's souls (see John 10:7-15). He has control over the elements of nature and the power to save men eternally. Still there were those who preferred to rely on false shepherds. 1. They turned to soothsayers and idols for rain. But those who do will find themselves without a real shepherd (see vv. 1-2). 2. Those who follow Christ, on the other hand, will find a God who cares for his people (see v. 3),
who uses them to carry out his purposes in the earth (see vv. 4-5), 3. and who will restore both Judah and Ephraim to their rightful place before the Lord (see vv. 6-12).
